title: Irreversible commit requires fresh Security revalidation
summary: v0.14 closes the TOCTOU gap between initial method admission and later irreversible publication. A continuation requires host evidence that work actually started; immediately before commit, exact staged-state/context identity and a fresh Security snapshot/assessment are required.
invariants: Initial Security ALLOW is not authority to commit later.
Security validation alone is not proof that staged work actually started.
Changed staged state or context invalidates commit evidence.
New adverse evidence can change commit from ALLOW to HOLD.
Successful commit validation is single-use and fail-closed under consumption races.
Access Permissions still separately decides the exact COMMIT method authority.

provenance.claim: v0.14 continuation/commit contract defines exact state/context freshness, start provenance and separate Permission authority.
Executable qualification proves state/context substitution, new account-takeover evidence, expiry and replay barriers.
